historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, Chapter: 'The Battle of Hunayn', the year is 630 AD. Saburi was a Christian tribe in the province of Kufa who accepted Islam after the Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) victory in the Battle of Hunayn. They were rewarded by the Prophet with the title 'Saburi' which means 'the patient ones'.
historical_references.context: Islamic Expansion and Campaigns under Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)

historical_references.reference: Al-Baladhuri's 'Ansab Al-Ashraf, Chapter: 'The Saburiyah', around 860 AD. The Saburiyah were a Christian tribe in the province of Kufa, who converted to Islam during the Caliphate of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz (717-720 AD). They were a powerful tribal confederation and gave their allegiance to the Umayyad Caliphate. They were rewarded with the title 'Saburiyah' which means 'patience and endurance'.
historical_references.context: Islamic Expansion and Political History under Umayyad Caliphate
